newsitem.title: UK: BP's Foinaven oil field delayed again for "months".
newsitem.headline: BP's Foinaven oil field delayed again for "months".

text.p: British Petroleum Plc's (BP) troubled Foinaven oil field west of the Shetland Islands is unlikely to start producing before late August after leaks were found during final testing, an official said on Tuesday.

Norwegian offshore services group Awilco ASA, which is supplying the Petrojarl production vessel for Foinaven, said in a statement on Monday it had been told by BP to expect a delay of about "three to four months."
"We haven't put a final date on it...but we expect that sort of order of delay," said a BP spokesman.
"It's going to be a matter of months."

BP said the latest delay, which has pushed back the project to well over a year behind schedule, resulted from the need to remove a subsea manifold and other equipment from the seabed for inspection and possible repair.
Extensive water pressure testing of the subsea manifold revealed the possibility that four out of 48 valves had faulty seals.
"BP's commitment to ensure environmentally responsible production west of Shetland is total," a spokesman said.
"We have therefore decided to recover the affected manifold from the seabed for full inspection and to take whatever corrective steps are necessary to give us complete confidence in the system."

Awilco, which completed the tie-in of the Petrojarl floating production and storage vessel at the field in April, said it would continue to receive $108,000 a day from BP, paid since its contract began on November 29 last year.
"Negotiations with BP will be undertaken concerning an increase of the waiting rate that Awilco receives until the start of production," Awilco said.
Foinaven, the first field to be developed in the waters of the Atlantic margin, was originally due on stream in June 1996 but has been dogged by a series of technical and weather-related delays.

Discovered some five years ago by BP in partnership with Royal Dutch/Shell Foinaven has estimated recoverable reserves of 250 million barrels and should reach peak output of 120,000 barrels per day (bpd).
